question: What are the main risks Apple describes about its supply chain and foreign exchange?

answer.summary: Apple's primary foreign exchange exposure relates to non-U.S. dollar-denominated sales, cost of sales and operating expenses worldwide, and gross margins on foreign-country products and on products containing components obtained from foreign suppliers have been and could in the future be materially adversely affected by FX fluctuations [T00221]. In FY2023, Services gross margin growth was partially offset by weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar and higher Services costs [T00333]. The retrieved evidence contains no dedicated supply chain risk factor beyond that FX factor's reference to foreign-sourced components [T00221]. On the revenue side, FY2023 revenue fell 2.8% to $383.29B [F00013], with Mac the largest contributor to the decline at -$10.82B (-26.9%), 98% of the total change [F00282], and Americas the largest segment contributor at -$7.10B (-4.2%), 64% of the total change [F00838]; Services grew $7.07B (+9.1%), moving against the decline and offsetting 64% of it [F00010]. Despite FX headwinds, gross margin percentage still rose to 44.1% in FY2023 from 43.3% in FY2022 [F01392].

Services moved against the decline, up $7.07B (+9.1%) to $85.20B (22.2% of total), offsetting 64% of the total change [F00010].
